keywords.rule: Counts are papers whose title or abstract contains one of the keyword's phrases (porter-stemmed, as the theme trends); the baseline is the papers in scope first submitted in the 12 weeks before the issue, its own papers excluded. new: fewer than 5 baseline papers; rising: at least 5 papers and a rate at least 1.5 times the baseline rate; hot: at least 15 papers (and 1% of the issue) at a rate at least 0.67 times the baseline rate; steady: otherwise.
keywords.score: log2(1 + n) · log2(1 + (n + 3) / (E + 3)), E = issue papers × (baseline papers with the phrase + 0.5) / baseline papers

keywords.name: Self-improving LLM agents

keywords.name: On-policy distillation

keywords.name: World models

themes.name: Agentic LLM systems and multi-agent orchestration
themes.summary: The papers build agentic LLM systems and multi-agent orchestration frameworks that coordinate specialized roles, self-improve through execution or reflection, and adapt over long-horizon tasks. They differ in focus: some synthesize training environments or agents, some allocate feedback or clarification, some evolve world models and harnesses, and others evaluate safety, retrieval, or orchestration policy.

themes.name: LLM reasoning, reinforcement learning, and test-time scaling
themes.summary: These papers study how to train and steer large language models for reasoning, spanning reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, on-policy distillation from teachers, and inference-time scaling via sampling and search. They differ in where they intervene: refining reward signals and credit assignment, reallocating supervision across trajectories or decision points, and improving samplers and test-time compute allocation.

themes.name: Mechanistic interpretability and explainability of neural networks
themes.summary: These papers decompose neural networks into interpretable internal components—circuits, attention heads, MLP neurons, sparse autoencoder features, and representation subspaces—and test whether those components actually explain model behavior. They differ in architecture (CNNs, ViTs, Mamba, diffusion and autoregressive transformers, LLMs, fMRI and geospatial models) and in methodology, ranging from circuit composition and attribution to causal interventions, gaze- and expert-based validation, and faithfulness auditing. A recurring concern is whether explanation methods identify the mechanisms they claim, motivating stress-tests, controls, and black-box causal audits.

themes.name: Vision-language-action models for robotic manipulation
themes.summary: These papers develop vision-language-action policies and world action models that ground visual, linguistic, and spatial understanding into robot control for manipulation, spanning whole-body dexterity, tactile grasping, stereo data generation, action tokenization, and policy adaptation. They differ in their learning source, drawing on human videos, egocentric demonstrations, synthetic or generated data, or robot data, and in their action interface, whether learned action tokens, latent actions, or constrained optimization. A further distinction is whether they augment policy learning with explicit future world-state, motion, or effect prediction versus relying on action supervision alone.

themes.name: Efficient LLM inference and inference-time compression
themes.summary: These papers address efficient LLM inference by compressing model weights, activations, KV caches, and token sequences, or by restructuring attention and decoding to reduce computation. They span quantization, token pruning and merging, KV-cache reuse and compression, and speculative decoding across language, speech, video, and multimodal models. They differ in whether efficiency is pursued through numerical precision, cache representation, token selection, or attention and decoding structure.

themes.name: Time-series foundation models and forecasting
themes.summary: These papers study time-series forecasting and foundation models, covering pretraining, covariate encoding, event forecasting, and efficiency through block skipping. They differ in their modeling focus, such as probabilistic uncertainty, domain-specific deployments, and whether they adapt pretrained models or train specialized deep learning architectures.

themes.name: Benchmarking and evaluation of multimodal and embodied agents
themes.summary: The papers in this theme introduce benchmarks and evaluation frameworks for multimodal and embodied agents, covering video-language temporal reasoning in driving, spatial grounding for vision-language-action models, misleading charts encountered by web agents, geospatial reasoning and constrained spatial editing, multi-view graph evidence composition, continual learning, long-horizon multi-robot task execution, dexterous laboratory manipulation, text rendering in video generation, and answer-grounding consistency in remote sensing VQA. Several papers focus on diagnosing specific failure modes, such as recovering occluded objects, reading squint text, preserving anaphoric constraints in motion generation, stereotyping in speech LLMs, and motion quality in VLA-driven manipulation, while others audit existing evaluation runs instead of relying on aggregate scores. They differ mainly in modality, environment, and evaluation target: real robots versus simulation, laboratories versus Minecraft versus urban driving, and synthetic versus production-derived data.

themes.name: Memory mechanisms for LLM and embodied agents
themes.summary: These papers study memory for large language model agents and embodied vision-language-action policies, proposing mechanisms that range from input-dependent readouts and time-delay or state-space sequence models for content-aware recall to supervisory, revisable, dual-stream, and neighborhood-aware memory layers for manipulation and long-horizon interaction. Others benchmark which memory modality embodied agents should retain, trace temporal evidence in multi-party conversations, and build memory at test time, while some analyze when a predictive state is sufficient for memory and whether recurrent networks need to be learned at all. They differ in whether memory is a learned sequence-model state, an external retrieval store, or a structured supervisory layer over a frozen policy.

themes.name: 3D Gaussian Splatting and neural scene reconstruction
themes.summary: The papers in this theme investigate 3D Gaussian Splatting and neural scene reconstruction from various angles, such as feedforward reconstruction, LiDAR-inertial fusion, semantic and measurable reconstruction, pruning and densification strategies, reflection modeling, and dynamic effects like water animation. They differ in their specific goals: some improve efficiency and scalability of 3D reconstruction, others enhance geometric accuracy or material properties, while some adapt segmentation and pose estimation for building inspection or food volume estimation.

themes.name: Video diffusion and generative video editing
themes.summary: These papers advance diffusion-based video generation along several fronts: faster autoregressive and bidirectional denoising, memory and geometry conditioning for world models and robot navigation, and correction or super-resolution of generated clips. A second group targets editing, including prompt-driven audio-visual editing, professional motion editing, target-frame inbetweening, and co-speech gesture portrait synthesis. A third strand focuses on protecting source images and videos from unauthorized image-to-video customization via adversarial or unlearnable perturbations, and on aligning generated motion with rewards or simulated trajectories.

themes.name: Federated learning with privacy and robustness
themes.summary: These papers address federated learning settings where the aggregation step must preserve client privacy while remaining resilient to malicious or Byzantine participants. They differ in mechanism: some build verifiable, Byzantine-robust or priority-constrained aggregation and detection schemes, others add formal differential privacy guarantees or distributionally robust objectives, and others pursue personalization through LoRA adapters, vision-language adapters, or socially fair clustering and unlearning.

themes.name: Stochastic optimization and variance reduction
themes.summary: The papers in this theme design and analyze stochastic optimization algorithms that reduce gradient estimation variance and improve stability, spanning variance-reduced policy gradient, adaptive variance reduction without oracle smoothness, randomized momentum transport with cheap predictors, and zeroth-order residual tracking for partially informed gradients. Others address stability of adversarial minimax optimization through control theory, geometry-aware and norm-constrained multi-objective oracles, and lower bounds for randomized linear-oracle optimization over strongly convex sets. They differ in the structure they exploit—importance sampling, momentum corrections, residual estimates, or norm pairs—and in whether they target deep learning optimizer benchmarking, bandit regret, or constrained nonsmooth nonconvex rates.

highlights.title: ProgramGym: Scaling Training Environments for Long-Horizon Program Reproduction Agents
highlights.authors: Chengyi Yang, Renxu Bao, Jue Hou et al.
highlights.theme: Agentic LLM systems and multi-agent orchestration
highlights.why: Provides 1,648 verifiable training environments across multiple languages and lifts a 27B coding agent from 34.87% to 42.84% on program reproduction, making scalable agent training useful.
highlights.key_result: ProgramGym was shown to improve program reproduction: Fine-tuning on trajectories with these constructed environments raises the performance of Qwen3.8-27B from 34.87% to 42.84%, and Program-Agent further raises the base and SFT models to 55.71% and 56.25%, both exceeding some flagship models.
evidence: Fine-tuning on trajectories with these constructed environments raises the performance of Qwen3.8-27B from 34.87% to 42.84%. Program-Agent further raises the base and SFT models to 55.71% and 56.25%, both exceeding some flagship models.

On ProgramBench, Qwen3.8-27B-SFT reaches 42.84% Tests Passed against 34.87% for Qwen3.8-27B ( =+7.97) and narrows the gap to DS-V4-Flash-0731 under the same agent scaffold (57.68%). The Qwen3.8-27B-SFT also exceeds the flagship GPT 5.4 result (37.70%) under mini-SWE-agent.

Program-Agent raises Qwen3.8-27B from 34.87% to 55.71% Tests Passed and Qwen3.8-27B-SFT from 42.84% to 56.25% relative to Claude Code. Each run exceeds Claude Opus 4.7 (50.90%) and Gemini 3.5 Flash (53.60%) under mini-SWE-agent.

highlights.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
highlights.authors: Taoyong Cui, Pinxian Zeng, Wanghan Xu et al.
highlights.theme: Agentic LLM systems and multi-agent orchestration
highlights.why: Demonstrates domain-general recursive self-improvement via world models, more than doubling lab-planning scores and achieving 96.15% reaction yield, with broad applicability.
highlights.key_result: RSI-Anything demonstrates substantial gains across diverse computational and scientific domains: in code repair, with the coder fixed, success increases from 26.3% with a static verifier to 29.2% through predictive selection and 31.2% after world-model adaptation, at comparable test usage; GUI evaluations showed higher task completion while average actions decrease by 39.4%; across five successive policy versions, laboratory-planning scores more than double from 21.80% to 46.01%; and in reaction optimization, RSI-Anything achieves 96.15% mean best observed yield versus 82.16% for Bayesian optimization under the same 40-experiment budget.
evidence: In code repair, with the coder fixed, success increases from 26.3% with a static verifier to 29.2% through predictive selection and 31.2% after world-model adaptation, at comparable test usage.
Graphical user interface (GUI) evaluations showed higher task completion, while average actions decrease by 39.4%.
Across five successive policy versions, laboratory-planning scores more than double from 21.80% to 46.01%.
In reaction optimization, RSI-Anything achieves 96.15% mean best observed yield versus 82.16% for Bayesian optimization under the same 40-experiment budget.
These results demonstrate how predictive world models and retained system updates enable recursive improvement across diverse environments.

highlights.title: Rethinking Relative Policy Differences Transfer of On-Policy Distillation
highlights.authors: Rong Wu, Daocheng Fu, Yu Yang et al.
highlights.theme: LLM reasoning, reinforcement learning, and test-time scaling
highlights.why: Systematically shows that a stronger teacher is not necessarily better for on-policy distillation, with task-specific differences transferring while scale-only differences do not, which can reshape training practice.
highlights.key_result: The paper shows that differences induced by task-specific training—including RL and SFT—transfer consistently (all task-optimized differences improve the target, with the RL and SFT pairs yielding G_T ranging from 9.78 to 32.23), whereas differences arising from model scale alone transfer weakly or not at all, with the proxy gain G_P strongly associated with the target gain G_T (Pearson r=0.96, Spearman ρ=0.93).
evidence: First, a stronger expert is not necessarily a better source of supervision: differences induced by task-specific training, including reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning, transfer consistently, whereas those arising from model scale alone transfer weakly or not at all.

All task-optimized differences improve the target: the RL and SFT pairs yield G_T ranging from 9.78 to 32.23, and Qwen3-4B-RL with an alternative Qwen3-1.7B reference achieves 25.85, showing that the reference need not be expert's training origin.
Across all pairs, the proxy gain G_P is strongly associated with the target gain G_T (Pearson r=0.96, Spearman =0.93; Figure ).

highlights.title: Fly-by-Code: Embodied Coding Agents for Aerial Manipulation with Active Visual and Physical Feedback
highlights.authors: Jaewoo Lee, Jeongyeon Seo, Sihyun Cho et al.
highlights.why: Active View-and-Probe feedback raises aerial manipulation success from 31.7% to 75% and transfers to a physical aerial manipulator, addressing key perception and interaction limits.
highlights.key_result: Across six simulated aerial manipulation tasks with 60 trials per condition, AF reduces false completion declarations from 25 to 5 and raises final task success from 31.7% to 75% compared with terminal feedback under the same coding-agent configuration and task-execution limit; using shared robot APIs, task programs refined with AF in simulation run on a physical aerial manipulator without task-program source-code modification and complete multi-stage manipulation tasks in the real world.
evidence: Across six simulated aerial manipulation tasks with 60 trials per condition, AF reduces false completion declarations from 25 to 5 and raises final task success from 31.7% to 75% compared with terminal feedback under the same coding-agent configuration and task-execution limit.

Using shared robot APIs, task programs refined with AF in simulation run on a physical aerial manipulator without task-program source-code modification and complete multi-stage manipulation tasks in the real world.
These results show that executable diagnosis fills gaps in execution feedback for embodied coding agents, improving both completion assessment and program refinement in aerial manipulation.

evidence: We deploy PanTact on a Unitree G1 humanoid without additional body contact sensors, demonstrating whole-body dexterity involving body support, pushing, sweeping, and load-sharing.
Performance: Ours (Upper-Body IK) achieves an 85% success rate, and Ours (Sparse Contact Tracker) achieves 80% (Fig. d). Occasional failures occur when the gripper misses the small object.

highlights.title: SWE-Duel: Towards a Self-Scaling Arena for Coding Agents
highlights.authors: Wei Minn, Zhensu Sun, Lwin Khin Shar et al.
highlights.theme: Agentic LLM systems and multi-agent orchestration
highlights.why: SWE-Duel's self-scaling arena creates evaluation tasks at runtime, preventing leakage and showing task difficulty scales with authoring capability, which is a promising direction for coding benchmarks.
highlights.key_result: In a 1,500-turn tournament among 11 participants, GPT-5.5 with Codex CLI was the strongest solver, repairing 98.3% of the defects it reviewed; Claude Opus 4.8 with mini-swe-agent was the strongest task author, with a 27.3% Red win rate.
evidence: We present SWE-Duel, an arena in which coding agents test each other. In a 1,500-turn tournament among 11 participants, GPT-5.5 with Codex CLI was the strongest solver, repairing 98.3% of the defects it reviewed. Claude Opus 4.8 with mini-swe-agent was the strongest task author, with a 27.3% Red win rate.

We run a tournament among 11 model–harness participants on 15 repositories in five languages for 1,500 turns. GPT-5.5 with Codex CLI ranks first as the strongest solver, repairing 98.3% of the defects it reviews. Claude Opus 4.8 with mini-swe-agent ranks second as the strongest task author, with a 27.3% Red win rate.

highlights.title: One Model to Loop Them All: Elastic Latent Recurrence for Language Models
highlights.authors: Faisal Ladhak, Shantanu Acharya, Santiago Akle Serano et al.
highlights.theme: Efficient LLM inference and inference-time compression
highlights.why: Elastic Latent Recurrence removes the one-loop tax of looped language models, yielding Koi-4B that matches Qwen3.5-4B at one loop and improves with more loops, enabling compute-adaptive inference.
highlights.key_result: We present Elastic Latent Recurrence (ELR), a recipe for training looped language models without this tax: at one loop, an ELR model costs the same to serve as a non-recurrent model of the same size and, trained on the same data, reaches similar accuracy. On 4B dense and 30B-A3B MoE hybrid models, ELR at one loop is 0.52 points below and 1.04 points above its matched baseline on a ten-task average, and four loops add 7.25 and 4.75 points; carried through post-training, the recipe yields Koi-4B, a single checkpoint that scores an estimated 18 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at one loop, matching Qwen3.5-4B, and 29 at four loops.

news.title: Sophos cuts threat investigation time by 96% with OpenAI Daybreak
news.summary: Sophos reported that using OpenAI Daybreak agents cut the average response time for cases using those agents from about 38 minutes to 89 seconds, a 96% reduction in investigation time, with 52% of MDR cases resolved end-to-end by AI. The text states Sophos protects more than 625,000 organisations, distils trillions of daily events from more than 500 third-party integrations into roughly 1,000 to 2,000 cases for nine security operations centres, and offers three MDR operating modes: Notify, Collaborate, and Authorise.

news.title: Asana cuts model costs 76x in browser tests with GPT-6.1 Sol
news.summary: Asana reported that using GPT-6 Astra in Codex to optimize its browser agent workflow on GPT-6.1 Sol made it 76x cheaper and 5x faster in a 144-run study, averaging $0.47 in estimated model costs and about four minutes per run versus the original production setup on Model B. The text says work estimated at one to two months by hand took about a week, and that the best-performing policy accumulated screenshots up to 20 before cutting back to the most recent one, tested with history budgets of 120,000 and 480,000 characters across six caching and screenshot policies run three times on each of four models.

news.title: Impactful scheduling for GPU clusters
news.summary: Ai2's AI Infrastructure team reported replacing a priority-based scheduler with a system including GPU time budgets, hierarchical fair-share allocation, and a time-slicing contract, shifting GPU time debates into an administrative budgeting process. The text states Ai2 manages thousands of NVIDIA H100, B200, and B300 GPUs in clusters of 88 to 1024 GPUs for about 150 internal researchers, with outstanding requests for 2-3x more GPUs than available, and that under the prior scheduler 100% of scheduled workloads eventually used HIGH priority.

news.title: ICYMI: What landed for AI builders in September 2026
news.summary: AWS recapped September 2026 updates across Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore, and Strands, including the public preview of Amazon Bedrock Managed Agents powered by OpenAI and the general availability of OpenAI's Astra, Sol, and Luna models on Amazon Bedrock, with GPT-6 Astra supporting up to 1 million input tokens. Other specifics: the Strands harness is an open source agent harness that AWS says uses 28 percent fewer tokens, and Strands Decider 2B is a 2B-parameter decision model delivering answers in ~115ms locally, with the AgentCore runtime getting lower cold start latency and sessions scaling to zero when idle.

news.title: How Postman runs Agent Mode for 40 million developers on Amazon Bedrock
news.summary: Postman described running its Agent Mode across API testing, documentation, discovery, and implementation on Amazon Bedrock for 40 million developers, using model flexibility, geographically scoped cross-Region inference, model-dependent zero data retention, and multi-tier prompt caching. The text says Agent Mode requires user approval before actions that modify application state and uses Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to redact personally identifiable information before it reaches the underlying LLM, addressing challenges such as tool sprawl and treating context as the primary bottleneck.

themes.name: 时间序列基础模型与预测

highlights.title: ProgramGym: Scaling Training Environments for Long-Horizon Program Reproduction Agents
highlights.authors: Chengyi Yang, Renxu Bao, Jue Hou et al.
highlights.theme: Agentic LLM systems and multi-agent orchestration
highlights.why: 提供 1,648 个跨多种语言的可验证训练环境，并将一个 27B 编码智能体在程序复现上的表现从 34.87% 提升到 42.84%，使可扩展的智能体训练变得实用。
highlights.key_result: ProgramGym 被证明能够改善程序复现：在这些构建的环境轨迹上进行微调，将 Qwen3.8-27B 的性能从 34.87% 提升到 42.84%，而 Program-Agent 进一步将基础模型和 SFT 模型提升到 55.71% 和 56.25%，两者均超过了一些旗舰模型。
evidence: Fine-tuning on trajectories with these constructed environments raises the performance of Qwen3.8-27B from 34.87% to 42.84%. Program-Agent further raises the base and SFT models to 55.71% and 56.25%, both exceeding some flagship models.

On ProgramBench, Qwen3.8-27B-SFT reaches 42.84% Tests Passed against 34.87% for Qwen3.8-27B ( =+7.97) and narrows the gap to DS-V4-Flash-0731 under the same agent scaffold (57.68%). The Qwen3.8-27B-SFT also exceeds the flagship GPT 5.4 result (37.70%) under mini-SWE-agent.

Program-Agent raises Qwen3.8-27B from 34.87% to 55.71% Tests Passed and Qwen3.8-27B-SFT from 42.84% to 56.25% relative to Claude Code. Each run exceeds Claude Opus 4.7 (50.90%) and Gemini 3.5 Flash (53.60%) under mini-SWE-agent.

highlights.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
highlights.authors: Taoyong Cui, Pinxian Zeng, Wanghan Xu et al.
highlights.theme: Agentic LLM systems and multi-agent orchestration
highlights.why: 通过世界模型展示了领域通用的递归自改进，将实验室规划得分翻倍以上，并实现了 96.15% 的反应产率，具有广泛的适用性。
highlights.key_result: RSI-Anything 在多个计算和科学领域展示了显著增益：在代码修复中，固定编码器的情况下，成功率从使用静态验证器的 26.3% 提升到通过预测选择的 29.2%，再到世界模型自适应后的 31.2%，且测试用量相当；GUI 评估显示任务完成率更高，同时平均动作数减少 39.4%；在五个连续的策略版本中，实验室规划得分从 21.80% 翻倍以上，达到 46.01%；在反应优化中，RSI-Anything 在相同的 40 次实验预算下实现了 96.15% 的平均最佳观测产率，而贝叶斯优化为 82.16%。
evidence: In code repair, with the coder fixed, success increases from 26.3% with a static verifier to 29.2% through predictive selection and 31.2% after world-model adaptation, at comparable test usage.
Graphical user interface (GUI) evaluations showed higher task completion, while average actions decrease by 39.4%.
Across five successive policy versions, laboratory-planning scores more than double from 21.80% to 46.01%.
In reaction optimization, RSI-Anything achieves 96.15% mean best observed yield versus 82.16% for Bayesian optimization under the same 40-experiment budget.
These results demonstrate how predictive world models and retained system updates enable recursive improvement across diverse environments.

highlights.title: Rethinking Relative Policy Differences Transfer of On-Policy Distillation
highlights.authors: Rong Wu, Daocheng Fu, Yu Yang et al.
highlights.theme: LLM reasoning, reinforcement learning, and test-time scaling
highlights.why: 系统地表明，对于 on-policy 蒸馏，更强的教师并不一定更好，任务特定差异可以迁移，而仅规模差异不能迁移，这可以重塑训练实践。
highlights.key_result: 本文表明，由任务特定训练（包括 RL 和 SFT）引起的差异会一致地迁移（所有任务优化的差异都改进了目标，其中 RL 和 SFT 配对的 G_T 范围为 9.78 到 32.23），而仅由模型规模引起的差异迁移很弱或根本不迁移，代理增益 G_P 与目标增益 G_T 强相关（Pearson r=0.96，Spearman ρ=0.93）。
evidence: First, a stronger expert is not necessarily a better source of supervision: differences induced by task-specific training, including reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning, transfer consistently, whereas those arising from model scale alone transfer weakly or not at all.

All task-optimized differences improve the target: the RL and SFT pairs yield G_T ranging from 9.78 to 32.23, and Qwen3-4B-RL with an alternative Qwen3-1.7B reference achieves 25.85, showing that the reference need not be expert's training origin.
Across all pairs, the proxy gain G_P is strongly associated with the target gain G_T (Pearson r=0.96, Spearman =0.93; Figure ).

highlights.title: Fly-by-Code: Embodied Coding Agents for Aerial Manipulation with Active Visual and Physical Feedback
highlights.authors: Jaewoo Lee, Jeongyeon Seo, Sihyun Cho et al.
highlights.why: 主动 View-and-Probe 反馈将空中操作成功率从 31.7% 提高到 75%，并迁移到物理空中机械臂，解决了关键的感知和交互限制。
highlights.key_result: 在六个模拟空中操作任务中，每个条件进行 60 次试验，与相同编码智能体配置和任务执行限制下的终端反馈相比，AF 将错误完成声明从 25 次减少到 5 次，并将最终任务成功率从 31.7% 提高到 75%；使用共享机器人 API，在仿真中用 AF 精炼的任务程序可以在物理空中机械臂上运行，无需修改任务程序源代码，并在现实世界中完成多阶段操作任务。
evidence: Across six simulated aerial manipulation tasks with 60 trials per condition, AF reduces false completion declarations from 25 to 5 and raises final task success from 31.7% to 75% compared with terminal feedback under the same coding-agent configuration and task-execution limit.

Using shared robot APIs, task programs refined with AF in simulation run on a physical aerial manipulator without task-program source-code modification and complete multi-stage manipulation tasks in the real world.
These results show that executable diagnosis fills gaps in execution feedback for embodied coding agents, improving both completion assessment and program refinement in aerial manipulation.

highlights.title: PanTact: Teaching Whole-Body Dexterity with a Wearable Contact Interface
highlights.authors: Xiaomeng Xu, Han Zhang, Zhian Ruan et al.
highlights.why: 从无机器人的可穿戴接触演示中实现全身人形机器人灵巧性，并部署在 Unitree G1 上，将操作能力扩展到手部之外。
highlights.key_result: PanTact 部署在 Unitree G1 人形机器人上，无需额外的身体接触传感器，展示了涉及身体支撑、推、扫和负载分担的全身灵巧性；在硬件上评估，Ours (Upper-Body IK) 在 Grasp-and-Embrace 上实现了 85% 的成功率，Ours (Sparse Contact Tracker) 实现了 80%，Ours (WBIK+Dense Tracker) 在 Sweep-and-Stow 上实现了 90.63% 的端到端成功率，在 Carry-and-Push 上实现了 90% 的成功率。
evidence: We deploy PanTact on a Unitree G1 humanoid without additional body contact sensors, demonstrating whole-body dexterity involving body support, pushing, sweeping, and load-sharing.
Performance: Ours (Upper-Body IK) achieves an 85% success rate, and Ours (Sparse Contact Tracker) achieves 80% (Fig. d). Occasional failures occur when the gripper misses the small object.

Performance: Ours (WBIK+Dense Tracker) achieves an end-to-end success rate of 90.63%. The robot sweeps with its wrist, forearm, or gripper side and closes the cabinet with either knee or a foot, adapting beyond the demonstrated forearm and left-knee contacts.
Performance: Ours (WBIK+Dense Tracker) achieves a 90% success rate. Failures occur when the robot drops the carried box, which happens more frequently with Ours (Sparse Tracker) and Humanoid UMI++.

highlights.title: CASTER: Formalizing Zero-Shot Manipulation from Synthetic Videos as Constrained Optimization
highlights.authors: Yinlong Dai, Homanga Bharadhwaj, and Dylan P. Losey
highlights.why: 将合成视频到机器人轨迹的迁移形式化为约束优化问题，并将平均任务成功率提高 34.1%，为真实人类演示提供了有原则的替代方案。
highlights.key_result: 在 12 个真实世界任务中，CASTER 实现了 76.6% 的平均零样本任务成功率，比最佳基线高出 34.1%。
evidence: Across 12 real-world tasks, CASTER achieves 76.6% average zero-shot task success, exceeding the best-performing baseline by 34.1%.

In our experiments we remove these simplifications to more closely match the underlying optimization, leading to more robust zero-shot trajectories from synthetic videos and improving average task success by 34.1% compared to the best-performing baseline.
Across the 12 tasks, CASTER achieved a higher average zero-shot success rate than the baselines.

highlights.title: SWE-Duel: Towards a Self-Scaling Arena for Coding Agents
highlights.authors: Wei Minn, Zhensu Sun, Lwin Khin Shar et al.
highlights.theme: Agentic LLM systems and multi-agent orchestration
highlights.why: SWE-Duel 的自扩展竞技场在运行时创建评估任务，防止泄漏，并表明任务难度随出题能力扩展，这是编码基准的一个有前景的方向。
highlights.key_result: 在 11 名参与者进行的 1,500 轮锦标赛中，配备 Codex CLI 的 GPT-5.5 是最强的求解器，修复了其审查的 98.3% 的缺陷；配备 mini-swe-agent 的 Claude Opus 4.8 是最强的任务作者，红方胜率为 27.3%。
evidence: We present SWE-Duel, an arena in which coding agents test each other. In a 1,500-turn tournament among 11 participants, GPT-5.5 with Codex CLI was the strongest solver, repairing 98.3% of the defects it reviewed. Claude Opus 4.8 with mini-swe-agent was the strongest task author, with a 27.3% Red win rate.

We run a tournament among 11 model–harness participants on 15 repositories in five languages for 1,500 turns. GPT-5.5 with Codex CLI ranks first as the strongest solver, repairing 98.3% of the defects it reviews. Claude Opus 4.8 with mini-swe-agent ranks second as the strongest task author, with a 27.3% Red win rate.

highlights.title: One Model to Loop Them All: Elastic Latent Recurrence for Language Models
highlights.authors: Faisal Ladhak, Shantanu Acharya, Santiago Akle Serano et al.
highlights.theme: Efficient LLM inference and inference-time compression
highlights.why: Elastic Latent Recurrence 消除了循环语言模型的单次循环代价，得到 Koi-4B，其在单次循环时与 Qwen3.5-4B 相当，并随着更多循环而改进，实现了计算自适应推理。
highlights.key_result: 我们提出了 Elastic Latent Recurrence (ELR)，这是一种训练循环语言模型且无需此代价的方案：在单次循环时，ELR 模型的服务成本与相同规模的非循环模型相同，并且在相同数据上训练时达到相似的准确率。在 4B 稠密和 30B-A3B MoE 混合模型上，单次循环的 ELR 在十任务平均分上分别比其匹配基线低 0.52 分和高 1.04 分，四次循环分别增加 7.25 和 4.75 分；经过后训练，该方案得到 Koi-4B，这是一个单一检查点，在单次循环时在 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 上的估计得分为 18，与 Qwen3.5-4B 相当，四次循环时为 29。
evidence: We present Elastic Latent Recurrence (ELR), a recipe for training looped language models without this tax.
At one loop, an ELR model costs the same to serve as a non-recurrent model of the same size and, trained on the same data, reaches similar accuracy.

On 4B dense and 30B-A3B MoE hybrid models, ELR at one loop is 0.52 points below and 1.04 points above its matched baseline on a ten-task average, and four loops add 7.25 and 4.75 points. Carried through post-training, the recipe yields Koi-4B, a single checkpoint that scores an estimated 18 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at one loop, matching Qwen3.5-4B, and 29 at four loops.

news.title: Sophos cuts threat investigation time by 96% with OpenAI Daybreak
news.summary: Sophos reported that using OpenAI Daybreak agents cut the average response time for cases using those agents from about 38 minutes to 89 seconds, a 96% reduction in investigation time, with 52% of MDR cases resolved end-to-end by AI. The text states Sophos protects more than 625,000 organisations, distils trillions of daily events from more than 500 third-party integrations into roughly 1,000 to 2,000 cases for nine security operations centres, and offers three MDR operating modes: Notify, Collaborate, and Authorise.

news.title: Asana cuts model costs 76x in browser tests with GPT-6.1 Sol
news.summary: Asana 报告称，在 Codex 中使用 GPT-6 Astra 来优化其在 GPT-6.1 Sol 上的浏览器智能体工作流，使其在 144 次运行的研究中便宜 76 倍，速度快 5 倍，平均估计模型成本为 $0.47，每次运行约四分钟，而 Model B 上的原始生产设置则不同。文中说，手工估计需要一到两个月的工作大约用了一周时间，并且表现最佳的策略累积了最多 20 张截图，然后削减到最近的一张，在 120,000 和 480,000 字符的历史预算下，对四种模型分别运行三次，测试了六种缓存和截图策略。

news.title: Impactful scheduling for GPU clusters
news.summary: Ai2 的 AI 基础设施团队报告称，用包括 GPU 时间预算、分层公平共享分配和时间切片合同的系统取代了基于优先级的调度器，将 GPU 时间争议转变为行政预算流程。文中指出，Ai2 为大约 150 名内部研究人员管理着数千个 NVIDIA H100、B200 和 B300 GPU，集群规模为 88 到 1024 个 GPU，未满足的 GPU 请求比可用量多 2-3 倍，并且在之前的调度器下，100% 的已调度工作负载最终使用了 HIGH 优先级。

news.title: ICYMI: What landed for AI builders in September 2026
news.summary: AWS recapped September 2026 updates across Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore, and Strands, including the public preview of Amazon Bedrock Managed Agents powered by OpenAI and the general availability of OpenAI's Astra, Sol, and Luna models on Amazon Bedrock, with GPT-6 Astra supporting up to 1 million input tokens. Other specifics: the Strands harness is an open source agent harness that AWS says uses 28 percent fewer tokens, and Strands Decider 2B is a 2B-parameter decision model delivering answers in ~115ms locally, with the AgentCore runtime getting lower cold start latency and sessions scaling to zero when idle.

news.title: How Postman runs Agent Mode for 40 million developers on Amazon Bedrock
news.summary: Postman 描述了在 Amazon Bedrock 上为 40 million 开发人员运行其 Agent Mode，涵盖 API 测试、文档、发现和实现，利用模型灵活性、地理范围的跨区域推理、模型相关的零数据保留和多层提示缓存。文中说 Agent Mode 在修改应用程序状态的操作之前需要用户批准，并使用 Amazon Bedrock Guardrails 在个人可识别信息到达底层 LLM 之前对其进行脱敏，以应对工具蔓延等挑战，并将上下文视为主要瓶颈。
